releaseNotes.title: Standby, AppIntents, iOS17
releaseNotes.description:
- Minimum iOS version requirement raised to iOS 16.
- Shortcut actions converted to App Intents for enhanced interaction.
- EasyMQTT widgets now supported in iOS 17's new "standby" mode.
- Under-the-hood architecture change to improve reliability and testability, with UI/UX enhancements.

items.title: The app won’t connect to my broker
items.text: First, try a known-good public broker like `broker.emqx.io` to confirm EasyMQTT can reach the network. If that works, check your host, port, username/password, MQTT version, and TLS settings. Most connection issues come from the wrong port, a TLS mismatch, or a stale client ID.

items.title: Where can I find MQTT error and status messages?
items.text: If you go to the **Settings** tab, there's a section for **App logs**. This is where EasyMQTT stores things like error messages from connecting to brokers or status messages from widgets and shortcuts running in the background.

items.title: What's the Client ID used for?
items.text: The client ID is used for the broker to identify the connecting client. Most brokers only allow one client with the same ID and will disconnect any other clients with the same ID. To get around that, in the **Settings** tab there's a way to set a **Device ID** which is used to uniquely identify your device.

items.title: I have some ideas/requests for new features, where can I submit those?
items.text: Feature requests can be discussed on the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/QYwjYEKFCp) or [via email](mailto:contact@easymqtt.app). Scroll down to the Contact section 👇

items.title: How do I configure Shortcuts?
items.text: You can create Shortcuts from the app or directly in the Shortcuts app. The easiest route is to press **+** in Shortcuts and search for **EasyMQTT**. You'll find actions for **Send Message**, **Send Favorite**, and **Fetch Message**.

items.title: Why can't I see any options for brokers?
items.text: Shortcuts only show brokers that are already saved in the app. Create or save the broker first from the **Connect** tab or **Settings → Brokers**, then it will appear in the Shortcuts picker.

items.title: Is it possible to trigger shortcuts from received MQTT messages?
items.text: Unfortunately due to some Shortcuts and background update limitations, triggering Shortcuts is not yet possible.

items.title: Can I send JSON payloads?
items.text: Yes. In Shortcuts, the payload is entered as text, so JSON payloads work well. For more complex payloads, it's easiest to build or format the text in another Shortcut step and pass it into EasyMQTT.

items.title: Why does my Fetch shortcut not receive anything?
items.text: Shortcuts only get a short time window to run, so the Fetch shortcut listens briefly and then completes. It works best with a topic that already has a **retained** message, because the broker can return the latest state immediately.

items.title: How do widgets work?
items.text: EasyMQTT widgets fetch data from a configured MQTT topic and display it in a glanceable format. Message widgets show the payload, while graph and multi-graph widgets plot numeric values over time.

items.title: What's the difference between Graph and Multi-graph widgets?
items.text: Graph widgets plot one MQTT value over time and can be configured directly on the Home Screen. Multi-graph widgets are part of EasyMQTT Plus, are created in the app, and can combine multiple graphs in one compact dashboard.

items.title: Why is my widget not updating/receiving data?
items.text: Widgets only get a short background refresh window, so it's best to use **retained** messages whenever you can. For graph widgets, the selected topic also needs to contain a numeric value that EasyMQTT can plot over time.

items.title: What's the property path?
items.text: The property path is how you tell your widget what exact value you want to display. Setting the property path to **payload** will display the whole message, setting it to **payload.temperature** will use only the temperature property (if available). Arrays are also supported and can be used in the following way: **payload.thermostats.[0].value**

items.title: How can I enable live updates of Multi-graph widgets?
items.text: To update multi-graph widgets live inside the app, subscribe to the same topics the widget uses. Once those topics are active, EasyMQTT can update the widget view as new values arrive.
